reason: Editorial read of all 68 built reward situations side by side, not a pattern scan. Silas, 2026-09-01: 'no awkward phrases or just bad text that doesn't communicate the objects intent? That's mostly what I care about... Are we being effective with what is being said?' Three defects the previous contract could not see. (1) best_used_when spends its sentence claiming the reward is useful, which the label already says -- 20 of 68. The prior check policed only the opening with a two-word window, so 'It proves most valuable when' walked through it, and telling the repair model to drop the opening frame simply moved it to the tail ('...is exactly the moment this ladle earns its keep'). The check now matches the claim wherever it sits. (2) Reward and location copy hard-codes the bundle's character ('It lets Bramble draft, stamp, and cross-reference...'), which welds an asset meant to be liftable into another story to one person; scenarios stay exempt by design. (3) Scenario setups open by naming our own schema: 'Under the dream vibe Sincerely, Wrongly Remembered, ...'. extra_fields carries two hand-picked editorial targets on 2026-08-07 that no honest regex generalizes: a local_rule whose second clause restates its first, and a best_scene that opens on 'The ghost-friend', a definite reference to someone never introduced. Re-filed after run 33463517245 aborted: the repair prompt's new no-schema rule read as "do not mention the vibe", so the model dropped the vibe title from the 2026-07-31 setup and failed validate_proposal's structural requirement that the setup name the vibe, location and character verbatim. Nothing was written -- the batch is all-or-nothing and the live phase never ran -- so this is a prompt fix, not a recovery. Both prompts and the complaint text itself now say to keep the title and drop only the schema noun, using the catalog's own "In <Vibe Title>, ..." opening that 30 of 34 built scenarios already use.
